entries.summary: Former JD Vance supporter says Vance’s “forever wars” talking points on Iran are getting tiring; argues Vance is talking in campaign phrases rather than as a serious thinker, and contrasts him with Marco Rubio.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Seed post from a long-standing verified account (created 2008, 183K followers). Engagement rate 1.06% of followers and 5.6% of views is in line for a mid-size political account, not an out-of-range spike. A sample of 11 original quote-posts showed a mix of agreement and pushback (roughly half supportive of the criticism), from mostly older accounts with custom avatars and modest followings. One newer digit-suffix account appeared in the sample. No copy-paste flood observed in the quotes opened.

entries.audience_sample: Of 11 original quotes opened, about half agreed with the criticism; several pushed back that the public does not want a prolonged Middle East war. Reply-to-like ratio 18%.

entries.summary: Writes that Vance, whom he once held in high esteem, surveyed the midterm “electoral massacre” and found “a scapegoat many others have found for millennia: the Jews,” calling it “rank cowardice.” Links his FrontPage Magazine column.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only, not proof. Verified pundit account (created 2009, 170K followers). 255K views and a 2.1% engagement rate vs. followers are high but plausible for a controversy post, not an inexplicable spike. A 25-reposter sample included many issue-aligned (pro-Israel) accounts, a mix of older and newer profiles, about 5 default avatars, several name-plus-digits handles, and at least one very new 2026 account with few followers and high posting volume. No identical copy-paste replies were documented in the sample opened. High reply-to-like ratio (28%) and a large opposing quote (Auron MacIntyre, 3,615 likes) indicate substantial pushback, not one-sided amplification.

entries.audience_sample: Quotes and replies are mixed. Notable pushback includes Auron MacIntyre’s quote-post (251K followers, 3,615 likes) rejecting the ‘Nazi’/scapegoat framing. Some quotes agreed with Hammer. Reposters leaned pro-Israel in bios.

entries.summary: Quotes Josh Hammer and says it “takes a very particular type of unhinged lunatic to publicly call the VP a Nazi because he acknowledged the Iran war was unpopular and responsible for the midterm loss.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Verified Blaze host/columnist account (created 2020, 251K followers). 1.4% engagement vs. followers and a low reply-to-like ratio (1.5%) are consistent with an aligned audience. No bot-like spike or copy-paste pattern was observed in the item opened.

entries.audience_sample: Low reply ratio (55 replies on 3,615 likes) suggests more agreement than argument in the sample of metrics, unlike the Hammer post it quotes.

entries.summary: Posts Vance’s line that “we told the American people we’d do no more forever wars,” then notes in parentheses that the Iran war has been going on for nearly nine months with no end in sight.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Established news-style account, 235K followers. Engagement is modest (0.14% of followers) and not out of line with a mid-size media account. No inauthentic-amplification signals were observed in the item opened.

entries.audience_sample: Reply-to-like ratio 12%; sample of replies/quotes not pulled for this item.

entries.summary: Amplifies Vance’s Fox interview comments that Trump will not let the Iran conflict become a “forever war,” quoting Vance that critics who want it to last “can attack me all they want.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Very large established account (4.0M followers). Engagement rate vs. followers is low (0.02%), typical for mega-accounts and not a suspicious spike. No bot-like pattern was observed in the item opened.

entries.audience_sample: Reply-to-like ratio 15%; replies not sampled in depth.

entries.summary: Calls an Iran-related agreement “a disaster,” saying it was “negotiated by VP Vance, promoted by VP Vance,” and adding “Notice you don’t defend it.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Long-standing official show account with 5.0M followers. Engagement rate vs. followers is low (0.12%), typical for a large account, not a spike. Reply-to-like ratio is only 7%, consistent with a relatively sympathetic audience. No inauthentic-amplification signals observed in the item opened.

entries.audience_sample: Relatively low reply-to-like ratio (7%) compared with more contested posts in this tracker.

entries.summary: Says the 2028 Republican primary is likely to be more crowded and competitive than some think, and that Tucker Carlson “will undoubtedly be a toxic and controversial issue tied to Vance.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Same official Levin account. Modest engagement for a 5M-follower account (0.01% of followers). No inauthentic-amplification signals observed.

entries.audience_sample: Reply-to-like ratio 13%; replies not sampled in depth.

entries.summary: Reports Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.) saying he will not back Vance in 2028. Quotes Fine that Vance’s post-election message was “abhorrent,” “smacked of the kind of thing you would read in 1932 Germany,” and that “He blamed the Jews for losing the election.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Small official-style reporter account (5.6K followers) but very high views (188K) and a 19.3% engagement rate vs. followers, which is high relative to the account size—plausible for a viral congressman quote, but the ratio is elevated. High reply-to-like ratio (42%) indicates heavy argument, not quiet amplification. Included because it reports a notable elected official, even though the reporter is under the 50K-follower guideline.

entries.audience_sample: Very high reply-to-like ratio (42%) indicates substantial pushback or debate. Replies were not fully coded.

entries.summary: Defends Vance against Rep. Fine’s antisemitism charge, saying Vance never mentioned Jews and cited pollster data on voters wanting to “change our relationship to Israel”—a country and foreign-policy question.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Large account (316K followers) posting similar defensive text in several replies the same afternoon—consistent with coordinated advocacy by one account, not a bot network. Engagement is low for the follower count (0.02%). Two smaller accounts posted nearly identical wording later; that copy-paste cluster is noted but those accounts were not added as entries (under the size cutoff).

entries.audience_sample: Very little discussion under this post (1 reply).

entries.summary: Argues that if Vance cannot say Trump made the right decision to disarm Iran, he has no business seeking the 2028 GOP nomination, and that if Vance can’t endorse Trump’s national security policy, Trump should not endorse him. Links his Washington Post op-ed.

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Verified columnist account (106K followers, created 2009). High engagement (5.6% of followers, 466K views) is large but consistent with a viral WaPo op-ed post. Reply-to-like ratio is very high (45%), which points to debate and pushback rather than one-sided inauthentic amplification.

entries.audience_sample: 1,560 replies on 3,497 likes (45%) is one of the most contested ratios in this set. Donald Trump Jr. replied with a screenshot of an earlier Thiessen column arguing there was “no U.S. downside to striking the Iranian regime.”

entries.summary: Replies to Marc Thiessen’s criticism of Vance with a screenshot of Thiessen’s earlier Washington Post opinion headline: “There is no U.S. downside to striking the Iranian regime.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. One of the largest political accounts on X (16.1M followers). Engagement rate vs. followers is low (0.04%), typical for a mega-account reply, not a suspicious spike. Image content was opened and is a WaPo headline screenshot.

entries.audience_sample: Reply-to-like ratio 12%; replies not fully coded.

entries.summary: Quotes Vance’s midterm postmortem and writes, “Every word of this is 💯💯💯.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Mega-account endorsement of the vice president’s own post. 6.57M views and 28,330 likes are large in absolute terms but a low rate vs. 16.1M followers (0.26%). A high reply-to-like ratio (35%) shows substantial argument under the endorsement, not only applause.

entries.audience_sample: 9,787 replies on 28,330 likes (35%) — heavy debate even on a supportive endorsement. Replies were not fully coded.

entries.summary: Writes that “the single biggest loser from last night’s massacre is JD Vance,” and that what followed is “the predictable repercussion of that new political reality.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Same verified pundit account. Engagement (1.3% of followers) is solid and not out of line. Replies/quotes were not sampled in depth for this earlier post.

entries.audience_sample: Reply-to-like ratio 8%; replies not sampled in depth.

entries.summary: Originating post. Vance says 2024 Trump/Vance voters showed up but many voted Democratic in 2026. Citing an unnamed pollster, he lists four reasons those voters gave for coming back: end the war; focus on cost of living/inflation; put America First; “Change our relationship to Israel.” He adds, “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”

authenticity.evidence: Heuristic only. Official vice-presidential account. Extraordinary absolute reach (73.5M views, 285K likes) with a high 7.3% engagement rate vs. 5.6M followers, consistent with a major post-election statement from a sitting VP, not a mid-tier account suddenly going viral. 69K replies and 21K quotes indicate a very large mixed conversation; those replies were not fully coded.

entries.audience_sample: Not coded in full (69,387 replies, 21,254 quotes). High absolute discussion volume. Donald Trump Jr. publicly endorsed the post.

entries.summary: Josh Hammer column, “JD Vance Scapegoats the Jews.” Argues Vance’s post-election claim that the Iran war and a changed U.S.-Israel relationship helped cause Republican losses amounted to blaming Jews or Israel. Hammer writes there is “zero intellectually honest case” that Israel specifically—as opposed to the Iran war generally—was a meaningful electoral factor.

authenticity.evidence: Outlet article. The frontpage URL was confirmed via the t.co redirect on Hammer’s post; the live page returned 403 to the fetch tool. Title and thesis were confirmed from that post and a Whatfinger reprint opened in search results.

entries.summary: Substack essay criticizing Josh Hammer’s “scapegoats the Jews” column and defending the idea that the Iran war and U.S.-Israel relationship were legitimately part of the midterm debate. Quotes Hammer’s claim that there is no honest case Israel was a factor, and disputes it.

authenticity.evidence: Independent Substack essay; page opened.

entries.summary: Leo Briceno reports that Rep. Randy Fine (R-Fla.) will not support Vance in 2028, saying the midterm postmortem “smacked of the kind of thing you’d read in 1932 Germany” and “He blamed the Jews for losing the election.” Notes Vance did not mention Jews specifically; Fine argues Israel and the Jewish people are inseparable and that three of Vance’s four points tacitly blamed “the Jews.” Vance’s office declined to respond.

authenticity.evidence: National outlet article; page opened.

entries.summary: GOP senators react skeptically to Vance’s midterm analysis. Sen. John Cornyn called the Israel/Iran explanation “ridiculous” and pointed to the economy. Sens. John Kennedy, Ron Johnson, and Thom Tillis also emphasized affordability, turnout, or tariffs. Ted Cruz said his view differs from Vance’s; Ted Budd asked what “change our relationship to Israel” means; Josh Hawley said the Iran war was “an issue” but not the only one.

authenticity.evidence: Trade-press article; page opened.

entries.summary: Doran argues Vance turned Trump’s Middle East strategy into a coalition liability by listing “change our relationship to Israel” separately from ending the Iran war, a phrase that can appeal both to mainstream restrainers and to the Groyper fringe. He asks whether Trump agrees, notes Trump Jr. endorsed Vance’s post, and says the movement may inherit a policy that treats the alliance as suspect.

authenticity.evidence: Think-tank essay; page opened.

entries.summary: Editorial says Vance must explain what he wants to change in U.S.-Israel relations and accept that the administration, not Israel, is responsible for U.S. war decisions. Notes an AP voter poll found about one-third said the Iran war was crucial to their vote, versus roughly half citing cost of living or corruption, so the war mattered but was not a complete explanation.

authenticity.evidence: Newspaper editorial; page opened.

entries.summary: Pro-Israel conservatives criticize Vance. CUFI Action Fund called him “clearly, demonstrably and unambiguously wrong” and said “the Jews were effectively blamed twice” via Israel and the Iran war, a “dog whistle.” Sid Rosenberg, quoted from X, called Vance “a disloyal, agenda driven problem” and urged replacing him as Iran negotiator with Marco Rubio. RJC board member Eric Levine said he did not recall exit polls identifying Israel as a voting factor. (Rosenberg’s original X post was not independently located in this pass.)

authenticity.evidence: Wire-service article; page opened.

entries.summary: Op-ed titled “JD Vance’s stunning act of disloyalty.” Argues Republicans lost in part because the Iran war dragged on and that “the vice president owns that.” Thiessen’s accompanying X post said Vance should not seek the 2028 nomination if he cannot say Trump made the right decision to disarm Iran.

authenticity.evidence: National newspaper op-ed; page opened (lead of the article).

entries.summary: News report on Vance’s midterm post. Notes Trump told reporters Vance’s war-and-gas-prices point was “largely true” but that he “would do it again” because Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. Quotes Jonathan Greenberg calling Vance’s comments “nonsense,” and notes Donald Trump Jr. backed the post with “Every word of this is 100 100 100.”

authenticity.evidence: Wire-service article; page opened.
